chapter_map.content: Chapter 6, Uniform Quantization Noise and exercises

proofs_and_claims_examined: code, distortion, block/vector quantizer, rate, and information definitions in Chapters 2-3
finite-alphabet and process rate-distortion definitions, finite-block converse, and negative coding theorem in Chapter 3
stationary-ergodic bounded-single-letter-distortion block-code achievability proof and its process-approximation premise in §3.4
finite-alphabet convexity, variational characterization, Shannon lower bounds, and the full stated Blahut updates/KKT conditions in Chapter 4
continuous-alphabet variational and Shannon lower bounds, vector/process bounds, and norm-distortion claims in Chapter 4

high-rate granular-cell approximation, overload decomposition, equivalent-sphere lower bound, point-density optimization, entropy approximation, lattice quantization, and their stated assumptions in Chapter 5
uniform-quantizer overload, dither, sigma-delta, and delta-modulation arguments and counterexamples in Chapter 6

limitations: Gray §4.4 explicitly declines to prove Blahut-algorithm convergence and cites Csiszár-Tusnády; this handoff includes a separate finite-alphabet proof rather than attributing one to Gray.

The continuous-alphabet variational extension in §4.5 is stated as a natural integral analogue and refers rigorous proofs to Csiszár; general existence, support, and integrability are not supplied by this citation.

The stationary Gaussian-process reverse-water-filling derivation is deferred to Berger/Gallager; the handoff states a bounded-spectrum sufficient regime and a proof route but does not claim Gray proves it.

Chapter 5 expressly calls its high-rate development less rigorous and assumes smooth density, small cells, fixed dimension, and negligible overload; its lower bounds are not automatically exact asymptotics or finite-rate guarantees.

The block-code achievability theorem in §3.4 assumes a stationary ergodic source and bounded additive single-letter distortion, and invokes a process-approximation lemma whose general proof is not given there. The unbounded MSE Gaussian case needs a different achievability argument.
